name: Ada
note: DoD language for large-scale and real-time systems; revised standard published as Ada 83
typeSystem: Static, very strong typing with strict range and subtype checking, no implicit conversions between distinct types, packages for encapsulation, and (since Ada 95) full object-oriented tagged types - designed from the outset to prevent whole classes of bugs common in safety-critical software.
runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native machine code; language-defined checks such as range, array-bounds, and null-access checks are normally inserted by the compiler. Pragma Suppress can selectively permit an implementation to omit checks, without requiring a proof and without requiring the implementation to omit them.

runtimes.name: Native (GNAT/GCC)
runtimes.role: GNAT, the GNU Ada compiler built on the GCC backend, is the most widely used implementation.

compilers.name: GNAT
compilers.role: GCC-based; the primary open-source and commercially supported Ada compiler.

concurrencyModel: Concurrency is part of the language itself: tasks and rendezvous were standardised in Ada 83, while Ada 95 added protected objects for coordinated access to shared data.
